speaker: Doctor
text: It is a little unusual, but I will proceed. Can you describe the rash's appearance, such as whether it is raised, scaly, or has a specific color? When did you first notice it?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. To narrow this down, does the rash involve the eyes, causing them to be red or purulent? Also, please describe if there is any fluid draining from the nose or ears.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Dermatitis. The history of maternal gonorrhea combined with a rash featuring pustules on an erythematous base sparing the palms and soles is pathognomonic. REQUEST TEST: Gram stain and culture of pustular fluid; REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin examination photos.
